This notebook asks whether a heat-pump conversion is a net contributor or a net cost to
MD BGE's delivery system under the current rate design. Starting from CAIRO master BAT
tables on S3, it diffs each non-heat-pump building's annual delivery revenue,
marginal-cost allocation, and grid electricity consumption between upgrade 00
(pre-retrofit) and upgrade 02 (post-retrofit).

The functions doing the data crunching live in
[`lib/rates_analysis/cos_funcs.py`](../../../lib/rates_analysis/cos_funcs.py) and
[`lib/rates_analysis/rate_case_funcs.py`](../../../lib/rates_analysis/rate_case_funcs.py).
This notebook just calls those with MD BGE's specific state/batch/scenario values from
`batch_config.yaml`.

## Setup

```{python}
#| label: setup

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

import polars as pl
import yaml
from great_tables import GT

from lib.great_tables import get_switchbox_gt_tab_options
from lib.quarto import display_gt
from lib.rates_analysis.cos_funcs import (
    bat_component_delta_with_gap,
    bat_component_summary_by_heating_type,
)
from lib.rates_analysis.rate_case_funcs import (
    add_heating_label,
    plot_weighted_bill_change_hist,
    plot_weighted_hist_by_group,
    segment_name,
)
```

## Parameters

Batch identity lives in `batch_config.yaml` alongside this report, not hardcoded here, so
re-running against a new batch is a one-file change. `UTILITY` matches the code
`analysis.qmd` uses for MD BGE.

```{python}
#| label: params

_batch_config = yaml.safe_load(Path("../batch_config.yaml").read_text())

STATE = _batch_config["STATE"]
BATCH = _batch_config["BATCH"]
DEFAULT_SCENARIO = _batch_config["BASELINE_BILL_SCENARIO"]
UTILITY = "bge"

SEG_DEFAULT_PRECALC = segment_name(DEFAULT_SCENARIO, "precalc")
SEG_DEFAULT_CALIBRATED = segment_name(DEFAULT_SCENARIO, "calibrated")

print(f"state={STATE}  utility={UTILITY}  batch={BATCH}  scenario={DEFAULT_SCENARIO}")
```

## Incremental delivery revenue vs. marginal cost

When a non-heat-pump home switches to a heat pump, its electricity consumption changes — and
so does its delivery bill. But does the *revenue* the utility collects from that home change
by more or less than the *marginal cost* that home actually imposes on the grid? The answer
tells us whether the conversion is a net contributor or a net cost to the delivery system
under the current rate design.

We compare each non-HP building's annual delivery revenue (`annual_bill_delivery`),
marginal-cost allocation (`economic_burden_delivery`), and grid electricity consumption
(`annual_kwh_grid`) between upgrade 00 (pre-retrofit, `default_precalc`) and upgrade 02
(post-retrofit, `default_calibrated`). We fetch every non-HP baseline heating type in one
pass rather than filtering to natural gas alone, since how the increment behaves differs by
heating type -- see below.

```{python}
#| label: bat-component-delta-data

bat_delta = bat_component_delta_with_gap(
    STATE,
    UTILITY,
    BATCH,
    SEG_DEFAULT_PRECALC,
    SEG_DEFAULT_CALIBRATED,
)
bat_delta.head()
```

Not every heating type gains electric load from a heat pump conversion. Homes already
heating with **electric resistance** typically see grid consumption *fall*, since a heat
pump is a much more efficient electric appliance replacing a much less efficient one; homes
switching from **combustion fuels** (natural gas, oil, propane) see grid consumption *rise*,
since the heat pump is new electric load. The table below breaks out average pre-retrofit
consumption, the average incremental change, and the average percent change in revenue and
marginal cost by baseline heating type, plus a $-per-incremental-kWh figure for both
revenue and marginal cost. That figure is a **weighted-sum ratio** (total incremental
dollars ÷ total incremental kWh across the group), not an average of each building's own
ratio -- a per-building ratio is unstable for any building whose incremental kWh is near
zero, which the weighted-sum approach avoids.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-bat-component-summary-by-heating-type
#| tbl-cap: "Average pre-retrofit consumption, incremental kWh, and incremental delivery revenue/marginal cost by baseline heating type after switching to a heat pump (MD BGE default rate)."

_bat_summary_by_heating_type = bat_component_summary_by_heating_type(bat_delta)
_bat_summary_gt = (
    GT(_bat_summary_by_heating_type, rowname_col="heating_type")
    .fmt_number(columns=["n_weighted", "avg_kwh_before", "avg_kwh_delta"], decimals=0)
    .fmt_currency(
        columns=["revenue_avg_before", "revenue_avg_delta", "mc_avg_before", "mc_avg_delta"],
        decimals=0,
    )
    .fmt_percent(columns=["revenue_pct_change", "mc_pct_change"], decimals=1)
    .fmt_currency(
        columns=["revenue_dollars_per_incremental_kwh", "mc_dollars_per_incremental_kwh"],
        decimals=3,
    )
    .cols_label(
        n_weighted="Weighted homes",
        avg_kwh_before="Avg. grid kWh before",
        avg_kwh_delta="Avg. Δ grid kWh",
        revenue_avg_before="Avg. revenue before",
        revenue_avg_delta="Avg. Δ revenue",
        revenue_pct_change="Δ revenue %",
        revenue_dollars_per_incremental_kwh="Revenue $/Δ kWh",
        mc_avg_before="Avg. MC before",
        mc_avg_delta="Avg. Δ MC",
        mc_pct_change="Δ MC %",
        mc_dollars_per_incremental_kwh="MC $/Δ kWh",
    )
    .tab_stubhead(label="Baseline heating type")
    .tab_spanner(label="Delivery revenue", columns=["revenue_avg_before", "revenue_avg_delta", "revenue_pct_change", "revenue_dollars_per_incremental_kwh"])
    .tab_spanner(label="Delivery marginal cost", columns=["mc_avg_before", "mc_avg_delta", "mc_pct_change", "mc_dollars_per_incremental_kwh"])
    .tab_source_note(
        "$/Δ kWh = weighted-sum incremental dollars ÷ weighted-sum incremental kWh for the "
        "group (not an average of each building's own ratio). MC = marginal cost."
    )
    .tab_options(**get_switchbox_gt_tab_options())
)
display_gt(_bat_summary_gt)
```

The sign flip is visible directly in the incremental-kWh distribution: electric-resistance
homes cluster on the negative side while combustion-heated homes cluster on the positive
side (@fig-hist-delta-kwh).

```{python}
#| label: fig-hist-delta-kwh
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of the change in annual grid electricity consumption per building after switching to a heat pump, by baseline heating type (MD BGE default rate)."

plot_weighted_hist_by_group(
    add_heating_label(bat_delta),
    "delta_annual_kwh_grid",
    "heating_label",
    "Change in grid kWh after HP retrofit, by baseline heating type",
    bin_width=250,
    x_label="Annual grid kWh change",
)
```

The remaining three figures show the population-wide (all non-HP heating types combined)
distribution of the dollar-denominated deltas underlying the table above.

```{python}
#| label: fig-hist-delta-delivery-revenue
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of the change in annual delivery revenue per building after switching to a heat pump, across all non-HP baseline heating types (MD BGE default rate)."

plot_weighted_bill_change_hist(
    bat_delta.select(pl.col("delta_annual_bill_delivery").alias("delta"), "weight"),
    "Change in delivery revenue after HP retrofit",
    show_mean_median=True,
)
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-hist-delta-delivery-mc
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of the change in annual delivery marginal-cost allocation per building after switching to a heat pump, across all non-HP baseline heating types (MD BGE default rate)."

plot_weighted_bill_change_hist(
    bat_delta.select(pl.col("delta_economic_burden_delivery").alias("delta"), "weight"),
    "Change in delivery marginal cost after HP retrofit",
    bin_width=25,
    show_mean_median=True,
)
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-hist-delta-delivery-revenue-by-heating-type
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of the change in annual delivery revenue per building after switching to a heat pump, faceted by baseline heating type (MD BGE default rate)."
plot_weighted_hist_by_group(
    add_heating_label(bat_delta),
    "delta_annual_bill_delivery",
    "heating_label",
    "Change in delivery revenue after HP retrofit, by baseline heating type",
    bin_width=100,
    x_label="Annual delivery revenue change",
)
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-hist-delta-revenue-minus-mc
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of incremental delivery revenue minus incremental marginal cost per building after switching to a heat pump, across all non-HP baseline heating types (MD BGE default rate). Positive values mean the utility collects more incremental revenue than the building's incremental cost — i.e. the conversion subsidizes other customers."

plot_weighted_bill_change_hist(
    bat_delta.select(pl.col("delta_gap").alias("delta"), "weight"),
    "Incremental delivery revenue minus marginal cost after HP retrofit",
    show_mean_median=True,
    x_label="Revenue minus marginal cost change",
)
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-hist-delta-revenue-minus-mc-by-heating-type
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of incremental delivery revenue minus incremental marginal cost per building after switching to a heat pump, faceted by baseline heating type (MD BGE default rate)."

plot_weighted_hist_by_group(
    add_heating_label(bat_delta),
    "delta_gap",
    "heating_label",
    "Incremental delivery revenue minus marginal cost after HP retrofit, by baseline heating type",
    bin_width=100,
    x_label="Revenue minus marginal cost change",
)
```
